text.p: Large-scale infrastructure projects that link utility and transport networks across continents will be the next driving force for engineering companies like Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, its president said.
"Borderless infrastrucure is the next big leap in our industry," Goran Lindahl said at the World Economic Forum, citing power and transport links as areas of major potential.

"I think in Europe this is well under way. If you take the electricity sector you see more and more cross-connections between countries," he told Reuters, noting links were also growing between Mediterranean Europe and North Africa.

"I visualise down the line you will have a grid around the Mediterranean and then you have a super grid structure up north, because investment in power generation is becoming more and more expensive."
High-speed railway lines across continents will also become more important to relieve overcrowding and help protect the environment, he said.

"If you take the railways, I don't think it is more than a decade away until we have railways going around northern Africa, crossing countries like Israel, Jordan, Turkey and crossing into Greece. I don't think it's too far away," he said.
He said society at large would have to finance the work by diverting existing funds into alternative uses and drawing on increased efficiency.
